units: <cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 1:1">Sabb. I, 1</cite>, sq. <he>פ׳ העני את ידו וכ׳</he> if the recipient puts his hand forth to within (the house).
<cite ref="Pesachim 118b">Pes. 118ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>שפּוֹשְׁטִין</he>, v. <cite ref="Q01222"><he>פַּס</he> II</cite>.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 28">Gen. R. s. 28</cite> <he>לא פָשְׁטוּ ידיהם במצות</he> they (the Sodomites) never stretched their hands forth for good deeds (charity); <cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 4">Lam. R. to IV, 6</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 351:1">Yalk. Ez. 351</cite>.
<cite ref="Berakhot 3b">Ber. 3ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Sanhedrin 16a:20">Snh. 16ᵃ</cite> <he>לכו פִשְׁטוּ וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="C00170"><he>גְּדוּד</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Menachot 1:2">Men. I, 2</cite> <he>פושט את אצבעותיו וכ׳</he> he stretches his fingers so as to reach his wrist.
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 2:9">Lev. R. s. 2</cite> <he>פושטין לו יד</he> we must reach forth our hands to him, v. <cite ref="K00873"><he>כָּנָף</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 13:5">Keth. XIII, 5</cite> <he>הפוסק … ופ׳ לו את הרגל</he> if a man promises a certain amount to his intended son-in-law, and shows him the foot, i.e. refuses to give it to him; a. v. fr.—

Y. R. Hash. III, 58ᵈ top (ref. to פשוט, ib. III, 3) כדי שיִפְשְׁטוּ וכ׳ (or שיְפַשְּׁטוּ, Pi.) (the horn is straight,) intimating that they must straighten their hearts through repentance.—Part. pass. פָּשׁוּט, q. v.
<cite ref="Mishnah Yoma 3:4">Yoma III, 4</cite>; <cite ref="Mishnah Yoma 3:6">6</cite>.
<cite ref="Yoma 31b:9">Ib. 31ᵇ</cite> <he>פּוֹשֵׁט … מקדש</he> he (the high priest) undresses first and then sanctifies (washes his hands and feet).

<cite ref="Yoma 32a:9">Ib. 32ᵃ</cite> <he>כלום אדם פושט אלא וכ׳</he> can a man put off anything except what he has put on? <cite ref="Mishnah Tamid 1:1">Tam. I, 1</cite>; a. fr.—Part. pass. <cite ref="Q02054"><he>פָּשׁוּט</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Yoma 3:6:3">Y. Yoma III, 40ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>אחת פ׳ ואחת לבוש וכ׳</he> whether he undresses or dresses, in either case the sanctification follows the act.

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 18">Num. R. s. 18</cite>; Tanḥ. Ḥuck. 1 <he>היה יושב ופושט וכ׳</he> was sitting at the gate of his town and explaining (teaching); (<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 10:7">Gen. R. s. 10</cite> <he>ודורש</he>).
<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 47">Ex. R. s. 47</cite> <he>היה למד … ופושט אותה וכ׳</he> he learned (the Torah) in day-time and explained it to himself at night; a. fr.—Part. pass. as ab.

<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 16">Lev. R. s. 16</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Psalms 34:13">Ps. XXXIV, 13</cite>) <he>כל ימי … היכן הוא פ׳</he> all my days I have read this verse (question), but I never knew where it is answered.
<cite ref="Horayot 3b:2">Hor. 3ᵇ</cite> <he>עד שתִּפְשׁוֹט הוראה בכל וכ׳</he> until the decision is spread (adopted) in the whole congregation of Israel.
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 36a:11">Ab. Zar. 36ᵃ</cite>; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to stretch, straighten out. Y. Snh. III, 21ᵃ bot. התחיל מְפַשֵּׁט וכ׳ (interch. with פישט) he began to put forth his hands and deal in fruits of the Sabbatical year.
units: <cite ref="Tosefta Negaim 1:8">Tosef. Neg. I, 8</cite> <he>מְפַשְּׁטִין את קומטיו וכ׳</he> the creases are straightened out, and then the leprous spot is examined; a. e.—

<cite ref="Tosefta Niddah 6:4">Tosef. Nidd. VI, 4</cite>, v. infra.—Part. pass. <he>מְפוּשָּׁט</he>. Y. Naz. IX, 57ᵈ <he>רגליו מְפוּשָּׁטוֹת וידו וכ׳</he> if the corpse is found with its feet stretched and its hands on the heart, opp. <cite ref="S01490"><he>קמצוץ</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Tosefta Kelim Kamma 4:17">Tosef. Kel. B. Kam. IV, 17</cite> <he>משיְפַשֵּׁט את חלוקו</he> (not <he>חלוקן</he>) from the time that the coat (the plaster of the stove) is taken off.

senses.gloss: to be straightened out, be unfolded, become flat.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 26:2">Kel. XXVI, 2</cite> <he>נ׳ טהור</he> when it (the bag) is straightened out (so as to be a plain piece of leather, v. <cite ref="Q02054"><he>פָּשׁוּט</he></cite>), it is not susceptible to uncleanness. Tosef. Neg. l. c. <he>כקמוט שנ׳</he> like a creased garment that has been straightened out; a. e.
<cite ref="Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 14:3">Pirké d’R. El. ch. XIV</cite> <he>נ׳ עור צפורן וכ׳</he> the horny skin was taken from Adam, and he saw himself naked.
<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 92">Midr. Till. to Ps. XCII</cite>, v. infra.

<cite ref="Mishnah Pesachim 5:9">Pes. V, 9</cite> <he>כיצד תולין ומַפְשִׁיטִין</he> how did they suspend and flay (the Passover lamb)? <cite ref="Mishnah Pesachim 5:9">Ib.</cite> <he>מי … ולהַפְשִׁיט</he> he that could find no place where to suspend and flay.
<cite ref="Mishnah Tamid 4:2">Tam. IV, 2</cite>.
<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 28:1">Pesik. R. s. 28</cite> <he>הִפְשִׁיטוּ את עבדיהם וכ׳</he> they undressed their men servants and maid servants and presented them &c.; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to shed the skin. Pirké d’R. El. l. c. שיהא מַפְשִׁיט את עורו וכ׳ that it (the serpent) should shed its skin once in seven years.
units: <cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 92">Midr. Till. to Ps. XCII</cite> <he>מן העור שה׳ הנחש וכ׳</he> ed. Bub. (oth. ed. <he>שנפשט</he>) of the skin which the serpent shed the Lord made garments of honor &c.; <cite ref="Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 20:9">Pirké d’R. El. ch. XX</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 34">Yalk. Gen. 34</cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Zevachim 11:3">Zeb. XI, 3</cite> <he>עד שלא ה׳</he> before the hide was taken off.
<cite ref="Zevachim 93b">Ib. 93ᵇ</cite>; a. e.

senses.gloss: to be straightened, become even; to flatten.
units: <cite ref="Chagigah 9a:13">Ḥag. 9ᵃ</cite> <he>חיגר … ונ׳ וכ׳</he> if he was lame on the first day and became straight &c. Y. Yeb. I, 2ᵈ bot. <he>עד שתִּתְפַּשֵּׁט הכף</he>, v. <cite ref="K00980"><he>כַּף</he></cite>; <cite ref="Tosefta Niddah 6:4">Tosef. Nidd. VI, 4</cite> <he>עד שתְּפַשֵּׁט את וכ׳</he>.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 120a:2">B. Bath. 120ᵃ</cite> <he>נִתְפַּשְּׁטוּ הקמטין וכ׳</he> the wrinkles became even, and her beauty returned &c.; a. e.
